deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a table of quadratic residues of primes p, i.e. the sets {x : (x/p) = +1}. The table starts on earlier folios and runs from p=277 on the previous page to p=383 on the next. No derivation is written out; each entry is the result of computing squares mod p (or Legendre symbols).

Layout and conventions (inferred from the whole run, consistent on every row):
- The sign above each prime is '+' when p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and '−' when p ≡ 3 (mod 4). It is therefore the value of (−1/p); it is not (2/p), because 317 and 349 are marked '+' although 2 is a nonresidue for them.
- The symbol before the list is '∓' for p ≡ 1 (mod 4), meaning both +x and −x are residues. Only residues x ≤ (p−1)/2 are then listed, and the row has exactly (p−1)/4 entries.
- For p ≡ 3 (mod 4) the symbol is '+', and all residues 1..p−1 are listed: (p−1)/2 entries.

Rows on this page:
- Lines 1–2: the tail of p=311 (≡3 mod 4), residues 196…300. The largest residue below 311 is 300 (= 4·3·25), since 310 is a nonresidue.
- p=313 (∓): 78 residues ≤156, ending with 155 and 156. Three blotted entries (after 132, after 147, after 152) are deletions: every number in those gaps is a nonresidue. '88' is a correction written above a blot.
- p=317 (∓): 79 residues ≤158, ending with 156 and 157.
  - Vertical bars stand after 39, after 79 and after 113. They mark p/8 ≈ 39.6, p/4 ≈ 79.25 and 3p/8 ≈ 118.9.
  - The same octant bars appear for 277, 281 and 293 on the previous page. Gauss was evidently splitting the residues into the intervals (kp/8, (k+1)p/8) to count them. Such counts are the quantities that enter class-number expressions for Q(√−p) and Q(√−2p) and the quartic-residue character of 2.
- p=331 (+): all 165 residues up to 329. The blot between 141 and 143 is a deleted 142, which is a nonresidue: (2/331) = −1 and (71/331) = +1.
- p=337 (∓): 84 residues ≤168.
- p=347 (+): 173 residues up to 345. The latter part is in a different (green/brown) ink with corrections:
  - 149 is inserted above a struck entry.
  - The struck entry after 152 is 153 (= 9·17, a nonresidue).
  - 197 is inserted.
- p=349 (∓): residues ≤174, last entry 171.
  - The cluster '82.[blot].85' is to be read as 83 then 85: 83 is a residue, while 82 and 84 are not.
  - '125' is inserted above, and the struck item after 126 is 127, which is a nonresidue.
- p=353 (∓): 88 residues ≤176. The '58/59' overwrite is 58: 59 is corrected to 58, since (59/353) = −1.

Method (implicit; my inference): the residues could be produced by listing x² mod p, or by multiplicativity from the characters of the primes, using quadratic reciprocity together with the supplements (−1/p) and (2/p). All my spot checks were done the second way.

Purpose: a large residue table, of the kind Gauss used for empirical work (cf. Disquisitiones art. 99–101 tables, Werke II tables). The octant marks suggest counts of residues in sub-intervals of (0, p/2).
errors: No arithmetic errors survive in the rows I checked: all 79 entries for 317 and all 78 for 313 were verified, plus numerous spot checks for 331, 337, 347, 349 and 353.

Gauss's own slips are visible but corrected by striking or overwriting:
- p=313: three entries are struck.
- p=331: 142 is struck.
- p=347: 153 is struck; 149 and 197 are inserted.
- p=349: an entry near 83/84 is blotted, and 127 is struck.
- p=353: 59 is overwritten to 58.

results.what: Table of quadratic residues mod primes 311 (tail), 313, 317, 331, 337, 347, 349, 353. For p ≡ 1 mod 4 only residues < p/2 are listed; marks encode (−1/p).
results.modern_name: Table of quadratic residues / Legendre symbol table
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, tables to 97); larger tables by Gauss and later Jacobi (Canon arithmeticus 1839)

results.what: Division points p/8, p/4, 3p/8 marked in the residue lists (here for p=317; also 277, 281, 293 on the previous page), presumably to count residues in octants of (0, p/2).
results.modern_name: Counting quadratic residues in intervals (kp/8, (k+1)p/8); related to class numbers h(−p), h(−2p) and to the quartic character of 2
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1839–40) for the class-number formulas expressed by such interval counts; Gauss is known to have studied such counts in his posthumous papers

deep.surprise_reason: This is a computational residue table of a kind Gauss is well known to have compiled. The octant markings hint at interval-count investigations that connect with class numbers, but the page contains only the raw data, not any formula.

checkable.asserts: The 313 row, with struck entries removed, is exactly the set of residues below 313/2.
The 317 row is exactly the set of residues below 317/2.

checkable.asserts: In the 349 row, 83 is the correct entry, 84 and 127 must be deleted, and 125 is correctly inserted.
The 59→58 overwrite in the 353 row is a correct correction.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.ntheory import legendre_symbol; (legendre_symbol(142,331), legendre_symbol(149,347), legendre_symbol(153,347), legendre_symbol(197,347)) == (-1,1,-1,1)

The '+'/'∓' marks coincide with (−1/p) = +1, i.e. p ≡ 1 mod 4.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.ntheory import legendre_symbol; max(x for x in range(1,311) if legendre_symbol(x,311)==1) == 309
checkable.asserts: Sanity check on the 311 tail. It returns 309 because 309 = 3·103 is a residue, so the listed tail ending at 300 omits some of the residues 301..309.

transcription_corrections: p=349: '83[?].84[?]' should read '83' only. The blot is a deleted entry; 84 is a nonresidue (84 = 4·3·7 with (7/349) = −1).
p=353: '58[?].59[?]' should read '58'. Gauss overwrote 59 with 8; 59 is a nonresidue.
p=331: the deleted item between 141 and 143 is 142 (a nonresidue); nothing should be inserted there.
p=313: the deletions after 132, after 147 and after 152 are struck entries, not lost residues. The row is complete with 78 entries.
p=317: the vertical bars after 39, 79 and 113 are octant markers at p/8, p/4 and 3p/8; they are not separators of the sequence.

Line 2: the 311 tail '...294.300' ends the 311 row on this page. A check (see checkable) shows 309 = 3·103 is also a residue mod 311, so the list either is incomplete beyond 300 or continues elsewhere; worth checking against the image.
